npcRoster.name: Bobbin Nosenil
npcRoster.publicDescription: Bobbin Nosenil is a Gandirosha tunnel criminal with a quick grin, quicker lies, and a habit of selling impossible jobs as if they were errands. She survives through charm, luck, secret passages, and the confidence that everyone else is either greedy, bored, or easier to fool than she is. Bobbin is funny until the cave-in starts; then it becomes clear her plans always reserve the safest exit for herself.
npcRoster.settlementAncestryTexture: Lunévaris is a Village in Lun’tharavé, under Participatory Democracy, with low danger, Farming, Beach and grass with water, Mountain range terrain, and public routes by Caravan, Train, Ferry, Steamship. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Gandirosha reads through the Fey-Folk entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Fey-Folk are peoples shaped by glamour, luck, tiny or otherworldly bodies, dreamlike emotion, and trickster magic. At my table, Faerie, Fairy, and Gandirosha are not separate top-level races here; they are bloodlines... Table cues: Fey Creature Type or Fey Ancestry, Fey Magic, Glamour or Luck Expression, Small/Tiny Fey Presence; starting tendency Neutral - Chaotic - Cooperative - Neutral.
publicRumors: Bobbin knows more sealed tunnels than the city engineers and fewer of them are legal.
She once sold the same hidden vault map to three crews and blamed the betrayal on bad ink.

npcRoster.name: The Brass Penitent
npcRoster.publicDescription: The Brass Penitent is a masked Verdan mechanist whose public voice promises safety while every private calculation is stained by the people their machines failed to protect. At the Lunevaris Transit Yard, they design containment automata, rescue constructs, and defensive protocols for the Regent Lattice, but their logic keeps circling one terrible conclusion: protection can become murder when compassion is reduced to efficiency. They are brilliant, theatrical, ashamed, and dangerous whenever guilt is allowed to write engineering doctrine.
npcRoster.settlementAncestryTexture: Lunévaris is a Village in Lun’tharavé, under Participatory Democracy, with low danger, Farming, Beach and grass with water, Mountain range terrain, and public routes by Caravan, Train, Ferry, Steamship. Verdan reads through the Verdan entry of the race compendium, within Orcs, Goblins, and Goblinoid Kin, marked by Enkirael. Fey-transformed humanoids who rapidly adapt physically and mentally as they age. They are resilient survivors with an unusually optimistic perspective on change. npcRoster.publicDescription:
Knight Swyn Vantaufo is a razor-tongued Dhampir watch knight with impeccable taste, lethal patience, and absolutely no interest in pretending to be nicer than she is. She is loyal with terrifying intensity once someone has earned his devotion, but strangers usually meet the cold ledger first: sarcastic, dismissive, judgmental, and very willing to remind people that politeness is optional but survival is not.
At the Neruvéa Archive, Swyn serves the Crucible Wardens as a night-watch enforcer, relic guard, and field interrogator for cases involving blood rites, undead contracts, ichor trafficking, and forbidden inheritance records. She has the old instincts of a predator and the discipline of a soldier, but his sharpest edge comes from contempt for weakness, hypocrisy, and anyone who mistakes glamour, beauty, or vice-district polish for softness.

npcRoster.name: Grond of the Milk-Oath
npcRoster.publicDescription:
Grond of the Milk-Oath is a blunt, towering Goliath warrior who mistakes poetry for literal instruction and believes “kindness” must be some hidden strength mortals drink, train, or beat into themselves. As one of Anubaldir’s giantkin, they value endurance, shared burden, direct conflict, and visible strength, but their travels slowly teach them that people survive through loyalty, settlement bonds, and fighting for those weaker than themselves.
At the Settlement Training Yard, Grond serves the Crucible Wardens as a siege companion and brutal defensive instructor, teaching recruits how to hold gates, break charges, and stop panicking when larger monsters hit the wall. They are loud, literal, battle-hungry, and often alarming, but their growing fascination with “the milk of mercy” makes them unexpectedly protective of civilians, chosen family, and any settlement that proves strength means standing together.

sourcePolicy.preserveOriginalProvinceRecords: The 29 overlapping province/distance JSON files were byte-identical between the geography-distance package and the province-area package, so the canonical records are retained and expanded in-place.
sourcePolicy.provinceAreas: Detailed province area records are attached by provinceKey and also preserved as separate files.
sourcePolicy.provinceGroupingExtensions: Four-province geographic links, all 20,475 four-province combinations, and province-pair distances are preserved in province_grouping_extensions and summarized into each province file.
sourcePolicy.settlementDescriptions: Descriptions are generated only from player-safe fields already present in the uploaded JSON: coordinates, sizes, terrain, races, factions, deities, danger, transit, and vertical profiles.

areaModel.method: Earth-sized spherical Voronoi province territory model
areaModel.reason: The province JSON files contain locked province center latitude/longitude coordinates, but no hand-drawn province border polygons. This model assigns every point on Belavadös to the nearest province center on an Earth-sized sphere, producing non-overlapping province territories whose areas sum exactly to the full planetary surface area in this model.
areaModel.boundaryNote: Boundary vertices are generated model borders between province centers, not hand-surveyed coastline or political-border artwork.
areaModel.precisionNote: Areas are model-exact for the spherical Voronoi territory model and rounded to 6 decimal places in output.

provinceDeepAtlasProfile.oneLine: Lun’tharavé is centered at -70.777906, 16.816239 under Participatory Democracy, with 35,306,000 people across 10 settlements.
provinceDeepAtlasProfile.extremeAtlasDescription: Lun’tharavé occupies 3,690,965.16 sq mi / 9,559,555.87 sq km of modeled Earth-sized territory, about 1.874181% of Belavadös's surface. It is not merely a province but a continent-scale civic machine: Beach and grass with water, Farming and Partial forest define its broad terrain, while its settlements intensify into Farming, Beach and grass with water and Beach and reefs with water. Population density is 3.693 people/sq km / 9.566 people/sq mi, which lets wilderness, roads, faction-held corridors, and vast uncrowded borders remain huge.
provinceDeepAtlasProfile.peopleFactionsAndFaith: The strongest public people-groups are Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage, Halfling and Smallfolk, Animalfolk and Mammalian Anthropomorphs, Elf Parent Race and Elf Bloodlines, Amphibious and Aquatic Peoples, Dwarven and Gnomish Kin, and 2 more. Frequently recorded peoples include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin, Harengon, Centaur, Giff, and 4 more. Faction visibility leans toward The Choral Synod, with worship and patronage records naming Nebyrr, Ishtanora, Iskareth, Bastveig, Sokhivar, Sigrananna, Marduthor, and 3 more.
provinceDeepAtlasProfile.groupLinkDescription: The province participates in 11 recorded four-province geography group links, including 8 cross-transportation-group links. These links place it inside overlapping regional corridors rather than one isolated block, allowing border-adjacent transit, faction influence, and cultural spillover to breathe across group lines.
